blocks.text: The reality of running a translation business

You are more than just a linguist. You are a business owner, a marketer, an accountant, and a project manager. This is the core problem. The translation profession has low barriers to entry, which creates intense competition. You must spend time on business development just to keep your pipeline full.

The constant switching between deep-focus translation and administrative tasks increases your cognitive load. You might be in the middle of a complex legal document and then get an email about an invoice. This shift breaks your flow state. It takes time to get back into the rhythm of your work.

The cost of poor organization is not just money. It is time, mental energy, and long-term career sustainability. When you spend too much time on low-value admin, you have less time for high-value translation work. This often leads to burnout, which affects nearly half of all translators at some point.

items: Focus on a niche field like medical or legal translation to stand out.
Build direct client relationships to gain more control over your rates.
Join professional bodies like the ITI or ATA to network and learn better business practices.
Use dedicated software for invoicing and project tracking to remove manual work.
Set specific blocks of time for admin work so it does not interrupt your translation sessions.

blocks.text: Organizing your Mac for translation work

The goal is to separate your translation workspace from your business workspace. You can use tools like SupaSidebar to create separate spaces for different projects. When you are in translation mode, your reference tools and CAT tools are front and center. When you are in business mode, your email, invoicing, and project management apps take over.

faq.question: How do I stop context switching?
faq.answer: Schedule your day in blocks. Keep admin and translation tasks separate. Use tools like SupaSidebar to hide non-essential tabs during your deep-focus hours.

faq.question: Why is business organization so hard for translators?
faq.answer: You are forced to wear many hats. You must be an expert in linguistics while also managing your own business, marketing, and accounting.

faq.question: Does joining a professional body really help?
faq.answer: Yes. Members of professional bodies like the ITI or ATA earn on average 30% more and report better overall wellbeing.
